findings.title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed to the repository
findings.body: The commit adds a gitlink/subproject file `sentry-repo` pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` without a `.gitmodules` entry. This looks like an accidentally staged nested checkout of the repository and will break `git submodule` commands or confuse tooling that clones the repository.

findings.title: Using Python's `hash()` in shared cache keys is non-deterministic across processes
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (line 27) and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 73) build cache keys using `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. In Python 3, `hash()` is salted per-process via `PYTHONHASHSEED` (although tuples of ints alone don't use the string salt, `hash()` is not guaranteed to be stable across Python versions, architectures, or interpreter invocations, and can also collide). More importantly, if `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is called from a different worker or environment than the one that populated the cache, or if two different project sets collide on their 64-bit hash, either invalidation will miss or an unrelated project set will inherit another project set's upsampling eligibility. Use a deterministic serialization (e.g., `,`.join(map(str, sorted(project_ids))) or a cryptographic digest like SHA-256) instead of `hash()`.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer `dataset` and `request` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query`
findings.body: In `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` and `request` rather than the `scoped_dataset` and `query` passed into `_get_event_stats`. During dashboard widget splitting (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset = discover` and modified queries such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"` while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_performance` / `metrics_enhanced_performance` and `request.GET["query"]` is unchanged. Because `dataset` is not `discover` or `errors`, upsampling will never be applied to split error widget queries, and even if `scoped_dataset` were passed, `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET.get("query")` rather than the `query` argument, so a transaction-split probe on a query containing `event.type:error` would still be treated as an error query.

findings.title: Substring check `"event.type:error" in query` misclassifies negated or compound queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `if "event.type:error" in query:` on the raw query string. This matches queries that are not restricted to error events—for example `!event.type:error`, `(event.type:error OR event.type:transaction)`, or a free-text search containing the literal `"event.type:error"`. When those queries run against the `discover` dataset for allowlisted projects, `count()` will be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` (`sum(sample_weight)`), producing wrong counts for non-error events (such as transactions, where `sample_weight` does not apply).

findings.title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling NULL/0 defaults for unsampled events
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, assuming `sample_weight` is populated for every event in an allowlisted project. In Snuba's errors/discover schema, events ingested before client error sampling was enabled or events sent without `client_sample_rate` have `sample_weight` unset (`NULL` or `0` depending on the table). Summing `sample_weight` directly instead of falling back to `1` per event (e.g., `if(greater(sample_weight, 0), sample_weight, 1)` or ` coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`) causes unsampled events in allowlisted projects to contribute `0` to `count()`, undercounting or returning `0`.

findings.title: Rewriting `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` breaks alias resolution and `topEvents` / `transformAliasToInputFormat`
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` replaces `"count()"` with `"upsampled_count() as count"`. However, the discover/errors query builder and `organization_events_stats` expect selected column expressions in Snuba/Discover syntax (e.g. `count()`), not SQL `AS` alias syntax, and when `transform_alias_to_input_format` is enabled (or in `top_events_timeseries`, where `orderby` or series keys look up the requested y-axis name `count()`), the returned alias or column parser will either fail to parse `upsampled_count() as count` or return results keyed under a different name than the requested `count()` y-axis.
